title: From Syndromes to Computation: A General Framework for Logical Operations in Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
authors: Hunter Nelson, Arshag Danageozian, ChunJun Cao, Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires error-correcting codes that not only protect quantum information but also support useful logical operations with practical physical realizations. Here we develop a general framework in which the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations directly organize logical-gate design. We derive an exact codespace-preservation condition valid at arbitrary rotation angles, providing a common stabilizer-level description for CSS and non-CSS codes and for both Clifford and non-Clifford operations. A particularly useful equal-syndrome specialization reduces Clifford gate design to stabilizer factorization, yields a general generator weight bound of $\lceil d/2\rceil$ for distance-$d$ codes, and systematically extends to logical rotations higher in the Clifford hierarchy. Applied to bivariate-bicycle (BB) and non-CSS Mirror qLDPC codes, the framework gives explicit low-weight Clifford and controlled-phase gates. Our implementations yield new low-weight gates, including an addressed $T$ gate on the $[[16,4,4]]$ BB code, $T$-type rotations on the $[[64,8,8]]$ BB code, and CCZ-, CS-, and $T$-type operations on the $[[36,6,6]]$ Mirror code. We also develop analytic constructions using Clifford algebra bases, which turn the syndrome constraints into explicit algebraic relations and provide a systematic route to logical addressability. We use this approach to analytically construct addressed CNOT, SWAP, controlled, and CCZ-type gates on recursive hypercube codes. An independent construction on middle quantum Reed--Muller codes yields C${}^r$Z gates that saturate the equal-syndrome weight bound. These results establish stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link between the stabilizer structure of a quantum code, the logical computations it can directly support, and the fault-tolerance properties of their physical realizations.
summary: This paper introduces a general, syndrome-based framework for designing fault-tolerant logical gates in quantum error-correcting codes. By relating logical operations directly to the stabilizer syndromes of physical Pauli rotations, the authors provide systematic methods to construct low-weight gates on various qLDPC codes. This advances the understanding of how code structure dictates computational capability.
main_problem: The paper develops a general framework to systematically design fault-tolerant logical quantum gates (both Clifford and non-Clifford) within Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECCs). It aims to unify the construction process beyond previous limitations.
main_result: The framework establishes stabilizer syndromes as a constructive link, allowing the explicit, low-weight construction of various logical gates (like addressed T gates and C^rZ gates) on specific codes such as BB and Mirror qLDPC codes.
method: The core method involves using the stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations to derive an exact codespace-preservation condition. This is supplemented by analytic constructions using Clifford algebra bases (CABs) to solve syndrome constraints.
model_or_system: The study focuses on stabilizer codes, particularly quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes like the Bivariate-Bicycle (BB) and Mirror codes, and the recursive hypercube construction. These codes are used to encode quantum information.
key_observables: Stabilizer syndromes, gate weight, code distance (d), and the resulting logical gate type (e.g., CNOT, T-gate).
important_parameters: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$, the general generator weight bound $\lceil d/2 ceil$, and the rotation angles for non-Clifford operations.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that logical operations can be systematically organized by analyzing the commutation relations (syndromes) of the physical Pauli rotations.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables summarizing bounded physical searches for logical gates on the $[[16, 4, 4]]$ and $[[64, 8, 8]]$ hypercube codes, grouping actions by family.
paper_structure: The paper develops the general syndrome-partition condition, applies it to existing qLDPC codes, utilizes analytic constructions via Clifford algebra bases, and finally examines the resulting fault-tolerance properties.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract coding theory, the systematic construction of logical gates is crucial for realizing any quantum computation, including those involving complex interactions relevant to AMO physics or quantum simulation.
